root_cause.text: In `rxrpc`'s `rxgk_verify_response()`, the bounds check validated only the XDR-rounded `token_len`, so rounding an attacker-controlled `token_len` before checking could overflow and let an oversized token length bypass packet-length validation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a new pre-check `if (token_len > len || xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len)` and the CVE/commit message explicitly states there was "a potential integer overflow due to rounding up token_len before checking it, thereby allowing the length check to be bypassed."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an explicit token length bounds check before rounded-size validation to reject malformed short packets safely.
intent_record.what: The packet length validation in rxgk_verify_response() was expanded from a single check of whether xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) exceeds len to an additional preliminary check that token_len itself is greater than len, using a two-part conditional before jumping to short_packet.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this causes packets to be rejected earlier when the declared token length alone already exceeds the available buffer length, preventing invalid or potentially overflow-prone length calculations from being treated as acceptable input and improving robustness of response parsing.

grouping_result.intent: Add an explicit token length bounds check before rounded-size validation to reject malformed short packets safely.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by validating the raw token length before applying XDR rounding, preventing overflow/bypass of packet-length checks for attacker-controlled oversized token lengths.

candidates.rationale: This is the flawed bounds check: it validates only the XDR-rounded token length. Because token_len is attacker-controlled, rounding it before validating the raw value can overflow and make an oversized token appear within bounds, allowing malformed packets to bypass length validation.
This statement loads the attacker-controlled token length that is later rounded and checked unsafely. It is part of the direct data flow enabling the overflow in the subsequent bounds check.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is fully visible in `rxgk_verify_response()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The root cause described is that validation checked only the XDR-rounded `token_len`, allowing overflow during `xdr_round_up(token_len)` to bypass the packet-length check. That exact construct is present here: `token_len = ntohl(rhdr.token_len); if (xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len) goto short_packet;` followed by `offset += xdr_round_up(token_len); len -= xdr_round_up(token_len);`. The attacker-controlled `token_len` is rounded before bounds validation, and the code does not first validate the unrounded `token_len` itself or guard against overflow in the rounded value/addition. This matches the stated bug pattern. No fix is present in this version: there is no separate check on raw `token_len`, no overflow-safe helper, and no validation ensuring both `token_len` and `xdr_round_up(token_len)` fit within `len` before advancing `offset`/`len`.

The vulnerable construct is present. Specifically, after reading `token_len = ntohl(rhdr.token_len);`, the code checks only the rounded length: `if (xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len) goto short_packet;` and then advances using the rounded value: `offset += xdr_round_up(token_len);` and `len -= xdr_round_up(token_len);`.
